How I use jev as a mathematics student:
For a new problem set, jev determines, for each problem, which sections of the lecture notes (definitions, theorems, etc.) are relevant.
Additionally, jev estimates the effort for each problem and identifies any dependencies between the problems.

Can you explain what jev brings to the party that indexing by tags fts5 search and vector databases don't do. Generally for searching metadata in images there are tried and trusted methods out there already. Perhaps where there is very extensive metadata with complex descriptions, this is where jev starts to become useful,  Short captions are probably best handled with word search.

Jev is amazing and fast. I created a skill "jev-router" to put in front of Claude Code. And used it to build a Chrome extension for analyzing web pages, social media posts, and even entire PDFs chapter by chapter on the developmental stage across nine different models of development. It does it so fast, so impressive. And because people are at different stages of development, I also built a translator for it to translate up or down taking the message from any of those sources and converting it into a message that can be understood and is compelling for people at different developmental stages. {Taking cues from the "Don't Mess with Texas" advertising story -- behavior changes more readily when the desired action reinforces the audience’s identity, which is stage dependent}. Still putting some finishing touches on it and plan to send it into the Chrome Web Store.
